pitch:mechanics-first.title: Low Tide Letters
pitch:mechanics-first.logline: In a fishing town that is slowly going silent, a twelve-year-old girl in her late grandfather's oversized raincoat follows a tin-can telephone string down a staircase the sea should never have uncovered, into the Lull: a bright crayon postal-world where every word anyone failed to say washes up alive. With two friends and a walking paper-boat letter who does not know who he is addressed to, she fights, or better, delivers, the town's unsent words using a battle system where feelings are sea-glass in your pockets: kept alone they warp you and eventually spill; handed to a friend they become twice as strong.
pitch:mechanics-first.theme_statement: What we do not say does not vanish; it waits. A feeling kept alone is sharp and heavy, and the same feeling told to a friend becomes smooth and strong. It is never too late to deliver a message, even to someone who is gone, and being loved does not require being remembered by name.
pitch:mechanics-first.hidden_truth:
Wren Ashby's grandfather, Pop Ansel Ashby, was the last keeper of Pellow's Reach lighthouse and later the town radio repairman. He lived next door, built the tin-can phone between his workshop and Wren's bedroom, and taught her to hunt sea-glass. When his memory began failing he labelled his whole house in shaky capitals (KETTLE, DOOR, WREN'S CHAIR). Last spring, at the care home Gull's Rest, he looked at eleven-year-old Wren, called her by her mother's name, and asked kindly who the little girl was. Wren ran out. For the last eleven weeks of his life she did not visit; she told her mum she had homework. On the final day she got as far as the car park and sat in the car. He died in August. She never said goodbye, never said sorry, and has told no one that she stayed away on purpose. She has worn his mustard raincoat every day since and has never once checked its pockets.

On one clear-headed afternoon Pop wrote her a letter and doodled in the margin what he always doodled for her: a little paper boat with legs. A nurse tucked it in his coat pocket; the coat came home in a bag. That unread letter is Pim, the fourth party member. He has been in her pocket the entire game (the menu entry 'Coat Pocket' reads: 'Nothing I want to look at.').

The Lull is where the whole town's unsaid words pool beneath the low-tide line. Wren's enormous unsaid thing sank into it and fed its caretaker, Auntie Mum, a gentle postmistress with a wax seal where her mouth should be, who is Wren's own avoidance given shape. She truly believes she is protecting children by keeping painful words sealed forever. As she grows, the real town goes quiet: each day more townsfolk speak only in '...'. Odo is hiding that his family's chip shop is closing and they move away in winter. Lin is hiding that she is exhausted and angry at raising her little brother alone while her mother works night boats. The letter's text, read in the best ending: 'Dear Wren. If I forget your name it is not because you were not worth remembering. You do not have to come and watch me go out like the tide. I would rather you were on the rocks finding glass. But if you come I will be glad, even if I cannot say who it is I am glad to see. Being loved does not need a name on it. Pop. P.S. The little boat is you. It has legs so it can always walk home.'
pitch:mechanics-first.emotional_arc: Minutes 0-5: a playable memory of tiny Wren and Pop sorting sea-glass in the sun (it is secretly the battle tutorial: 'Red for cross, blue for fretting, amber for fond, green for well-I-never. Don't keep them all in one pocket, love, you'll rattle.'), then a hard cut to the present: the too-big coat on its hook, labels still stuck around the house, and Odo's voice buzzing through a tin can: 'Wren? You awake? Over.' Warmth, a small ache, a joke. Chapters 1-3: delight and oddness; the Lull is funny and colourful, and the player learns that confiding in friends is literally the strongest move. Helping Odo and Lin say their unsaid things shows Wren (and the player) what it costs and what it gives. Chapter 4: dread and tenderness; the descending lighthouse is built from Pop's fraying memory, the friends learn what Wren did, and she freezes. They do not leave. Chapter 5: temptation; Auntie Mum offers painless quiet. Epilogue: release. The arc moves from 'if I never say it, it never happened' to 'saying it late still counts'.
pitch:mechanics-first.protagonist: Wren Ashby, 12. Watchful, dry-humoured, stubborn, answers questions with shrugs; kind in deeds rather than words. The player chooses her lines at 'Say it / Keep it' moments; otherwise she speaks little. Visual: small and slight; chestnut-brown bob she cut herself with kitchen scissors, uneven fringe, one tuft sticking out on the left; dark round eyes, freckles across the nose, a plaster on her chin. Wears Pop's mustard-yellow fisherman's raincoat, far too big, sleeves rolled four times, hem at her shins, one toggle missing; grey-and-navy striped jumper underneath; dark teal leggings; scuffed red wellington boots. Signature item: a dented tin can on a loop of white string worn across her body like a satchel. In the real world the coat is drawn dull ochre in pencil; in the Lull it is blazing crayon yellow and the can glows faintly from inside. Home colour: Blue (Worry). Battle role: flexible all-rounder and best at Say; weapon is the tin can swung on its string. Skills: Can Clonk (1 Blue, hit + lower enemy attack 20%), Hold the Line (2 Blue, party takes -30% damage for 2 turns), Beachcomb (1 Green, find a random raw glass for an ally), Plain Words (1 any Tumbled, a Say that cannot be Misheard), Rattle (1 Red + 1 Blue, heavy hit, +50% if Wren is below half Heart), Over-and-Out (Duet with Odo), Tide Table (Duet with Lin).
party_members: Odo Brill, 11. Wren's next-door neighbour, son of Brill's Chippy. Loud, boastful, generous, narrates his own life in radio procedure ('Commencing snack. Over.'), secretly afraid of the dark and of being left out. Arc: he brags because he cannot say the small true thing: the chippy is closing and his family moves inland in winter. He learns that telling friends bad news does not make it more real, only less lonely. Role: tank and Red generator; draws hits with Oi!, converts Red into big single-target damage. Home colour: Red (Temper). Skills: Oi! (free taunt, 2 turns), Cannonball (2 Red, heavy hit), Chip Shield (1 Amber, block next hit on an ally), Big Talk (1 Red, party +15% damage 3 turns), Salt and Vinegar (1 Red + 1 Green, hit all, 30% chance to lower defence), Whistle Blast (1 Blue, interrupt an enemy charge-up). Visual: short, stocky, round-faced; warm brown skin; black hair buzzed short; gap between front teeth; thick eyebrows. Bright orange foam life vest worn over a teal hoodie, navy shorts in all weather, grey socks, white trainers with orange laces, a scab on each knee. Signature item: a wire chip-shop fry scoop carried like a sword, plus a red plastic whistle on a lanyard.

Linnet 'Lin' Hale, 13. Class prefect, planner, carrier of spare tissues, corrects grammar mid-battle; speaks in lists. Arc: she is the grown-up of her house and is furious and tired underneath the competence; she has never once said 'I need help.' She learns to be looked after and to do one thing badly on purpose. Role: healer/support and pocket-manager. Home colour: Amber (Fondness), with a hidden well of Red. Skills: Plaster (1 Amber, heal 35%), Cup of Tea (2 Amber, heal party 25% and cure Sealed slots), Re-file (free once per battle, rearrange all glass between two allies), Red Pen (1 Red, hit + strip enemy buffs), Checklist (1 Green, the next 3 party actions each get +10% stacking), I Need Help (unlocks after Ch3; 1 Tumbled Red, every ally immediately Passes her one glass for free and she heals 50%). Visual: tall and thin with excellent posture; pale brown skin; very long black plait to her waist tied with a moss-green ribbon; round wire glasses; navy school cardigan with tan elbow patches over a white collared shirt, pleated charcoal skirt, grey knee socks with the left one always slipped down, black buckle shoes. Signature item: a wooden clipboard holding a tide table, pencil behind her right ear.

Pim. A knee-high unsent letter who woke up in the Lull with no address on him and is cheerfully determined to find out who he is for. Nosy, literal-minded, reads everyone else's mail aloud, terrible at secrets, proud of his stamp. Arc: he is Pop's letter to Wren. He slowly realises it (he keeps finishing Wren's sentences; he knows where the good sea-glass is) and in the finale chooses to be opened, which means ceasing to be Pim and becoming what he was always meant to be: read. Role: trickster/scout and Green generator; Listens twice per action, moves first, fragile. Home colour: Green (Wonder). Skills: Nosy (free, Listen reveals 2 Knot slots), Paper Cut (1 Green, fast hit, high crit), Fold (1 Blue, dodge next attack), Forward Mail (1 Green, move one glass from any ally to any ally and Tumble it), Origami (2 Green, copy the last skill an ally used at 70%), Special Delivery (1 Tumbled any, a Say that fills 2 matching slots). Visual: a cream-coloured envelope folded into a lopsided paper-boat body, two stubby black ink-line legs with no feet, no arms (he gestures by flapping his flap), two dot eyes and a tiny curved ink mouth, round wax-red cheeks, a torn top corner that sticks up like a cowlick. Signature item: a single pale-blue postage stamp showing a lighthouse, stuck crookedly on his forehead like a cap badge.
pitch:mechanics-first.world_structure:
Two layers, alternating Day then Night across three days.

PELLOW'S REACH (real world, no combat, 3 maps): drawn in soft graphite and grey-blue pencil with only a few objects coloured (the yellow coat, Odo's vest, the red postbox). Maps: Harbour Row (ground: cobbles, wet tarmac, grass verge; props: terraced houses, postbox, lobster pots, Brill's Chippy front, washing lines, tin-can strings between windows), Wren's House interior (floorboards, rug; props: furniture each wearing one of Pop's labels), and Shingle Beach with the Tide Steps (shingle, wet sand, rock; props: groynes, rock pools, upturned boat, the locked lighthouse on its spit). Each Day holds three 'Say it / Keep it' moments in conversation. Anything Said gives that friend a permanent starting Tumbled glass in every battle. Anything Kept spawns a named optional Unsent in that night's area (harder night, extra Keepsake). Each day more townsfolk speak only in '...'.

THE LULL (8 maps): full saturated crayon and coloured pencil on cream paper. Reached at night: the sea withdraws impossibly far, the tin-can string leads down stone Tide Steps into the seabed. Areas: 1) Sorting Shallows (ground: pale sand, ankle-deep turquoise water, envelope-paper tiles; props: cliff-high pigeonholes, mail sacks, stamp-flowers, rock-pool save points). 2) Penny Pier, two maps (ground: painted boardwalk planks, candy-striped carpet; props: carousel of seahorses, prize stalls, helter-skelter, speaking-tube pipes, bulb signs); everything loud so nobody has to talk. 3) The Hall of Shoulds, two maps (ground: green lino, parquet, carbon paper; props: filing cabinets to the ceiling, clocks, in-trays, a broken compliment vending machine, ironing boards). 4) Down the Lighthouse, two maps (ground: spiral stone, floorboards, fog; props: murmuring radios, mislabelled furniture, a care-home corridor door, a fogged car park with one car) spiralling down instead of up. 5) The Seal Office (ground: red carpet, dark wood, cooling wax; props: sealed doors, candle rows, a vast counter, drawers of other children's sealed letters). Rock pools are save points and let you 'Skim': rearrange raw glass between party members before fights. Enemies are visible on the map; no random encounters.
chapter_outline: Prologue, 'Glass' (3 min): playable memory on the rocks with Pop; he teaches the four colours and whistles his seven-note tune. Cut to the coat on its hook, the labelled house, and Odo's uninvited tin-can line: 'The sea's gone out too far. Like WAY too far. Over.'

Ch1, 'The Sea Went Out Too Far' (12 min): Day 1 on Harbour Row; first Say it/Keep it moments; Lin insists on supervising. Night: down the Tide Steps into the Sorting Shallows. Pim is found wedged upside-down in a pigeonhole, legs kicking. First Deliver tutorial (a Thank-You Card That Waited Too Long). Letter-sorting puzzle. Mini-boss: Postmaster Gull, a union-rules seagull who refuses any letter without an address.

Ch2, 'Penny Pier' (16 min): Day 2, the chippy has a CLOSING DOWN sign face-down in the back room; Odo changes the subject. Night: a funfair running at full volume with no riders. Whisper Tubes puzzle. Odo keeps volunteering for the front. Boss: Bigmouth Barker, a megaphone-headed showman who shouts over every Pass. Delivering him requires Odo to Say one Tumbled Blue: 'We're moving. I didn't want it to be true. Over.'

Ch3, 'The Hall of Shoulds' (16 min): Day 3 morning, Lin is late for the first time ever; half the town says only '...'. Night: endless filing office of tide tables and lists. Clock puzzle solved by deliberately setting one clock wrong and taking the door marked LATE. CG: Lin asleep on a stack of lists under Odo's life vest. Boss: Perfectly Fine, a tower of ironed laundry with a smiling paper mask; her Knot only accepts Red from Lin. Lin learns 'I Need Help'.

Ch4, 'Down the Lighthouse' (18 min): the string leads into a lighthouse that spirals downward. Radios murmur Pop's half-sentences. Relabel-the-room puzzle using what the player remembers from Wren's real house. Pim begins finishing Wren's sentences. At the care-home door Wren's pocket is force-filled with five Blue: a scripted Freeze Up. The player controls Odo, Lin and Pim, and the only way forward is to Pass glass to her, one each. The friends learn the truth in the fogged car park. Nobody leaves.

Ch5, 'Auntie Mum' (14 min): the Seal Office. Wax-door sequence puzzle. Auntie Mum offers to keep the letter safe forever (Ending C trigger). Boss fight: she Seals pocket slots and returns Passed glass 'to sender'. Then the final encounter, The Empty Chair: Strike does 0; a 7-slot Knot that needs glass Passed from all three friends, and a last slot only Pim can fill by being opened (Ending A) or that Wren may leave open (Ending B).
Epilogue (5 min): dawn, the tide comes in over the Tide Steps; ending scenes, credits over the Delivered Mail album, post-credits letter.
pitch:mechanics-first.emotion_mechanic:
POCKETS AND SEA-GLASS (replaces MP; no emotion triangle, no strengths/weaknesses wheel). Each party member has a Pocket of 5 slots shown as a row of sea-glass in the sand at their feet. Four colours: Amber = Fondness, Blue = Worry, Red = Temper, Green = Wonder. HP is called Heart and is drawn as a length of string.

GAINING GLASS (feelings happen to you): start of your turn +1 of your home colour (Wren Blue, Odo Red, Lin Amber, Pim Green). Being hit: +1 Blue. Seeing an ally lose 25% or more Heart in one hit, or drop: +1 Red. Being healed, shielded or guarded by an ally: +1 Amber. Using Listen, or seeing an enemy move for the first time: +1 Green. If the Pocket is full, the oldest raw piece is pushed out.

HOLDING RAW GLASS changes you, per piece: Red +8% damage dealt and +8% damage taken. Blue -8% damage taken and -8% damage dealt. Amber +10% healing given and received. Green +6% crit and accuracy. So a pocket full of Worry makes a timid wall; a pocket of Temper makes a glass cannon.

SPILL: if all 5 slots hold the same raw colour the character Spills for 2 turns and cannot be controlled. Red 'Lash Out': attacks a random target, allies included, at +50%. Blue 'Freeze Up': cannot act, takes -50% damage. Amber 'Cling': only heals the lowest-Heart ally. Green 'Drift Off': skips turns, 50% dodge. Afterwards the Pocket empties. Several enemies try to stuff you toward a Spill.

PASS (the core verb): once per turn, as a free action before their main action, each character may hand one glass to any ally with a free slot. A Passed piece becomes TUMBLED (drawn smooth, rounded, shining): it counts as 2 pieces of its colour when spent, carries no stat penalty (bonuses only), and never counts toward a Spill. A one-line confession flashes as it is handed over ('Odo: ...I was kinda scared back there. Over.'). A skill paid for entirely with Tumbled glass fires its OUT LOUD version: +50% effect plus a rider (e.g. Plaster Out Loud also removes debuffs; Cannonball Out Loud cannot miss and staggers). Every Pass between two characters adds 1 Bond to that pair; at 10 Bond the pair unlocks its Duet skill (6 Duets total, e.g. Wren+Odo 'Over-and-Out': costs 1 Tumbled Red + 1 Tumbled Blue, massive hit and Odo guards Wren next turn; Lin+Pim 'Registered Post': a Say that cannot shake loose). At 25 total Bond Wren gains a 6th slot.

MAIN ACTIONS: Strike (free, no glass), Skill (costs listed glass; 26 skills total), Listen, Say, Brace (-50% damage and cover one ally, who gains Amber), Item. Turn order by Speed; a preview ribbon of the next six turns runs down the right edge. Clear decision every turn: what do I Pass, to whom, and do I spend glass on power or on being heard?

SCREEN LAYOUT: side-on 'tideline' view. Enemies stand in the upper two-thirds on the battle background, each with its Knot drawn as a real rope knot with coloured loops above its head. The party stands as full-body sprites in a row along a strip of wet sand at the bottom, Pockets at their feet, Heart-strings beneath. Commands fan out as paper luggage tags from the active character. Passed glass is visibly skimmed along the sand between friends.
pitch:mechanics-first.nonviolent_mechanic: DELIVERING. Every enemy is an Unsent: a message someone never sent, alive and upset. Each has a Knot of hidden slots (regulars 2-3, bosses 5-7), each slot wanting one colour: what the message needed to be said with. LISTEN reveals one slot (Pim reveals two) and grants Green; slots can also be deduced from the enemy's muttering and look (one grumbling 'it's not FAIR' wants Red). SAY offers one glass from your Pocket to a matching slot. A Tumbled piece fills the slot and also calms the enemy so it skips its next attack. A wrong colour is Misheard: the glass is lost and the enemy gains +25% attack for 2 turns. Dealing damage to an enemy shakes loose its most recently filled slot, so you cannot comfortably do both. Fill every slot and the Unsent is DELIVERED: it unfolds into a paper gull and flies up out of frame. You receive its Keepsake (an accessory or consumable), Stamps (currency), +2 Bond for every pair, and its letter is added to the Delivered Mail album, a readable two-line story (sixteen tiny stories about the town). Reducing an enemy to 0 Heart instead HUSHES it: it crumples into a grey pebble and you receive Grit, which raises Level (Heart and Strike power). Both paths are viable and progress you differently: Grit makes you tough; Delivery makes you close (Duets, Out Loud, sixth slot, best accessories). The real cost: Say spends the same glass that powers your skills, so kindness is paid for in the resource you would otherwise hit with. Bosses add personal slots that only one specific character can fill, and only with Tumbled glass, meaning that character must first have been confided in. The final encounter cannot be damaged at all.
pitch:mechanics-first.antagonistic_force: Auntie Mum, Postmistress of the Lull ('mum's the word'). Very tall, stooped, gentle; a long dove-grey postal dress with brass buttons, a lavender shawl, white gloves, hair in a grey bun skewered with a letter-opener, soft kind eyes, and a round red wax seal where her mouth should be. She speaks by handing out small printed cards. She is not cruel: she is avoidance itself, born from the town's habit of keeping quiet and grown huge on Wren's secret. Her offer is sincere and tempting: 'Let me keep it for you, dear. It will never hurt. It will never anything.' Her servants are Sealing Wax Drips. Her power is making children comfortable. The true final obstacle is not her but The Empty Chair: a vinyl care-home visitor's chair in a foggy car park, with a small yellow raincoat folded on it.
endings: ENDING A, 'Delivered' (best). Conditions: Bigmouth Barker, Perfectly Fine and Auntie Mum all Delivered rather than Hushed; at The Empty Chair fill all 7 slots, and choose 'Open him' when Pim asks 'I think I know who I'm for. Is that all right?'. Pim unfolds in light; the letter is read in full, in Pop's handwriting, with the boat-with-legs doodle in the margin. Dawn at the lighthouse with Odo and Lin; Wren says aloud, to the sea, 'I'm sorry I stopped coming. I'm here now.' The tide comes in, the town's speech returns, Odo tells everyone he is moving and Lin's mum takes a day shift. Post-credits: a real stamped letter from Odo arrives with a terrible drawing of all four of them. The Coat Pocket menu entry now reads: 'A letter. Read often.'

ENDING B, 'Not Yet' (neutral). Conditions: any one of the three bosses Hushed, OR the player chooses 'Keep him' at Pim's question. The Empty Chair fades with six of seven loops filled. Pim stays in the Lull as a friend who waves from the bottom step. The town mostly recovers. Wren visits the churchyard with her mum and manages one sentence. The letter stays unopened, but the Coat Pocket entry changes to: 'Not yet. But soon.' The game is explicit that not-yet is allowed. Loading the cleared save lets the player return to the final choice.

ENDING C, 'Hush' (sad). Conditions: accept Auntie Mum's offer in Ch5, OR Hush all bosses and at least 60% of all encounters. Wren hands over the letter; it is sealed in a drawer among hundreds of others. The Lull goes perfectly calm and beautiful. She wakes light and untroubled; the town is polite and quiet; every label in the house is blank and she cannot recall why that bothers her. Final beat: the tin can rattles. 'Wren? You awake? Over.' One last Say it / Keep it prompt. Choosing Say it gives the line '...Odo? I think I forgot something important. Over.' and unlocks New Game Plus with the Bond between Wren and Odo carried over: a friend on the line is always a way back.
signature_images: CG1: tiny Wren on Pop's knee on sunlit rocks, both squinting through a piece of amber sea-glass held up to the sun; his big hand, her small one.
CG2: moonlit beach with the sea drawn back for miles; a stone staircase descending into the seabed; three small figures at the top and a white string trailing down into the dark.
CG3: Pim wedged upside-down in a cliff of pigeonholes, ink legs kicking, stamp askew, while Odo salutes him.
CG4: Penny Pier blazing with bulbs at night, every ride turning, not one rider; the three children tiny in the entrance arch.
CG5: Lin asleep against a tower of lists with Odo's orange life vest laid over her and Wren holding a finger to her lips at Pim.
CG6: a fogged car park with painted bays; one vinyl visitor's chair under a lamp; a small yellow raincoat folded on the seat.
CG7: Auntie Mum kneeling to child height, white-gloved hands open, wax-seal face, the kindest eyes in the game; behind her, a wall of tiny sealed drawers.
CG8: Pim unfolding into a sheet of lit paper, handwriting appearing line by line, the boat-with-legs doodle in the margin wearing a little blue stamp.
CG9: dawn on the lighthouse gallery; three children shoulder to shoulder, the letter in Wren's hands, the tide finally coming in, a paper gull overhead.
CG10 (Ending C): Wren's hallway in flat pretty pastel, every label on every object perfectly blank, the tin can on the windowsill trembling on its string.
enemy_concepts: Sorry-Not-Sorry: a crumpled apology note shaped like a crab that only scuttles sideways around the point. Knot: Red, Amber.
Thank-You Card That Waited Too Long: wilted greeting card in a sagging party hat, mortified. Knot: Amber, Amber. Tutorial Delivery.
Draft No. 47: a blushing note that crosses itself out and rewrites every turn (its visible slots reshuffle unless Listened). Knot: Green, Amber, Blue.
Reply-All: a flock of six identical memo-gulls; hitting one angers all; one shared Knot.
Chain Letter: a paper-chain snake promising seven years of bad luck; stuffs Blue into pockets to force Freeze Up.
Candyfloss Fib: a little white lie as a pink sugar cloud with a sticky grin; its attacks add Amber toward a Cling spill. Knot: Green, Red.
Penny Dreadful: a coin-slot fortune booth dealing doom cards; its prediction comes true next turn unless someone Braces.
Toot: a party horn that bellows I'M FINE; shows an Amber loop that is a decoy over a Red one.
Blank Postcard: 'Wish you were here' with nothing else written; mirrors whichever colour your party holds most.
Overdue Notice: a stern library slip with a rubber-stamp hammer; damage rises each turn it is ignored.
Listworm: an inchworm made of a to-do list that grows a segment and a Knot slot every 2 turns; Deliver it fast.
Pocket Lint: giggling fluff gremlins that steal Tumbled glass and run; Hush or Deliver them to get it back.
Wrong Label: a gentle teacup labelled DOOR that swaps the colours in your Pocket; it apologises constantly. Knot: Blue, Amber.
Static: a valve radio murmuring half of one of Pop's sentences; its Knot changes each turn until Listened twice; Delivering it completes the sentence.
Sealing Wax Drip: Auntie Mum's red wax blobs; Seal one pocket slot for 3 turns (cured by Cup of Tea).

BOSSES: Postmaster Gull (mini; rejects any Say that is not Tumbled: 'No return address, no service'); Bigmouth Barker (megaphone-headed showman in a striped blazer; his shouting cancels one Pass per turn until Odo whistles); Perfectly Fine (tower of ironed laundry with a smiling paper mask that cracks as Lin's Red is Said); Auntie Mum (Seals slots, sends Passed glass back to sender, offers a free full heal each turn that Hushes one of your glass); The Empty Chair (cannot be damaged, does not attack; each turn it fills Wren's pocket with Blue, and only friends' Passes keep her from freezing).
pitch:mechanics-first.exploration_and_puzzles: Loop: Day (5-8 min in town: talk, three Say it/Keep it moments, spend Stamps at Brill's Chippy on items such as Bag of Chips, Mushy Peas, Pickled Egg 'restores Heart; nobody is happy about it', Flask of Tea, Stick of Rock, Scraps) then Night (15-20 min Lull area with visible roaming Unsents, one puzzle, rock-pool saves with Skim, hidden sea-glass charms, a boss). Each area has a mail-slot shortcut back to the Tide Steps. Puzzles: 1) Sorting Shallows: read six stray letters and post each into the pigeonhole of its feeling colour; teaches the colour language used by every Knot. 2) Whisper Tubes (Penny Pier): rotate speaking-tube segments so a whispered message reaches the far booth unmangled; wrong routes produce funny garbles ('We're moving' arrives as 'Weird muffin'). 3) The Four Clocks (Hall of Shoulds): Lin's tide table gives the perfect settings, which open nothing; setting one clock deliberately wrong opens the door marked LATE. 4) Relabel the Room (Down the Lighthouse): furniture carries wrong labels; restore them from the player's memory of Wren's real house in the prologue, with WREN'S CHAIR placed last. 5) String Line (lighthouse cellar, dark): push posts to run tin-can string across the room; when taut you hear a friend's voice giving the next hint. 6) Wax Doors (Seal Office): each door opens to a colour sequence hidden in the printed cards Auntie Mum has handed you all game. Collectibles: 16 Delivered Mail letters, 12 sea-glass charms, 6 Duets, and the named optional Unsents spawned by Kept choices.
pitch:mechanics-first.humor_and_charm: Odo narrates everything in radio procedure and awards himself medals. Lin corrects enemy spelling mid-fight and keeps minutes of boss battles. Pim reads private mail aloud, believes stamps are a rank, and introduces himself as 'First Class'. NPCs: Second-Class Stan, a snail postman forty years into one delivery ('nearly there'); Shelley, a hermit-crab shopkeeper living in a red postbox who sells through the slot; a seagull union permanently on strike with placards reading SQUAWK; a compliment vending machine in the Hall of Shoulds that has been Out of Order for years and, once fixed, says only 'You're doing fine.' Item text is dry and fond. The Reply-All enemy apologises to everyone for the previous Reply-All. Pass confessions are often tiny and silly ('Lin: I do not actually like tea.'), so the heavy ones land.
pitch:mechanics-first.music_direction: Leitmotif 'Pop's Whistle': a seven-note phrase, G A C' A G E D, which never resolves to the home note C until Ending A. 13 tracks: 1 Title 'Low Tide' (solo music box, tape wobble, leitmotif unresolved). 2 'Harbour Row' (ukulele-style nylon plucks, glockenspiel, brushed kit; grows sparser each Day as the town falls quiet). 3 'Sorting Shallows' (celesta arpeggios, warm square lead, soft choir pad). 4 'Penny Pier' (waltzing fairground organ and saw lead, leitmotif at double speed, slightly out of tune). 5 'The Hall of Shoulds' (clock-tick percussion, pizzicato strings, prim piano in 5/4). 6 'Down the Lighthouse' (detuned piano, radio static, leitmotif played backwards on music box). 7 Battle 'Rattle Your Pockets' (bouncy bass, square lead, glock hits on every Pass). 8 Boss 'Out Loud' (driving kit, saw lead, string stabs; leitmotif in minor). 9 'Auntie Mum' (lullaby celesta over a too-sweet choir pad; every phrase ends cut short, sealed). 10 'The Empty Chair' (single held string note and a slow heartbeat kick; one instrument enters for each friend's Pass). 11 'Rock Pool' (save theme: nylon guitar, four bars). 12 'Dear Wren' (piano and strings; leitmotif finally resolves to C). 13 Credits 'It Has Legs So It Can Walk Home' (full band reprise with ukulele and whistled melody). Lo-fi post: gentle tape saturation, slow wow and flutter, vinyl crackle at low level, low-pass around 9 kHz. About 25 SFX: tin-can clank, glass clink for gain, smooth skim-and-chime for Pass, paper unfold and gull cry for Delivery, dull crumple for Hush, wax stamp thud for Seal, kettle-rattle warning one glass before a Spill, tag flick for menus, wave wash for transitions.
pitch:mechanics-first.originality_notes: Versus OMORI: no dream-friends who are figments, no shut-in, no sibling death, no concealed killing; the friends are real and physically present, the secret is an absence (visits not made) rather than an act. The battle system is not an emotion triangle with status buffs: feelings are a spendable, passable pocket resource with no rock-paper-scissors, a Spill risk, and a Tumbled state created only by confiding. Layout is a side-on tideline with full-body sprites and pockets in the sand, not four corner portraits. Versus Undertale: no underground of monsters, no fallen human, no bullet-hell; the peaceful route is not ACT-then-spare but a deduction-and-resource puzzle (Listen, then pay matching glass into a Knot) that competes with your own skills for the same currency; fighting is not framed as murder, and levels and bonds are both legitimate growth. Versus End Roll: no drug trial, no punishment dream, no guilt meter driven by kills; the other world is a communal place shared by a whole town. Versus Ib: no gallery, no paintings, no roses-as-life; the visual motif is post, paper and sea-glass, and companions are never pitted against each other. Versus Re:Kinder: no pact among children, no town-wide violence; the threat is silence and comfort, and the antagonist is gentle. Wholly original hooks: the Say it/Keep it day loop that spawns the night's enemies, the Pass/Tumble confiding economy, enemies as literal unsent messages with readable letters, and a party member who is the unread letter in the protagonist's own coat pocket.

pitch:heart-first.title: LOST LETTER CLUB
pitch:heart-first.logline: Eleven-year-old Nell Tarrow has just moved into the flat above a closed-down seaside sorting office. Under her bed is a shoebox of nine letters from the best friend she laughed at, which she has never opened. Every night she slides down the mail chute into the Sorting, a bright crayon world where undelivered messages come alive. With a club of lost letters she learns to say the one thing she keeps swallowing.
pitch:heart-first.theme_statement: The wound is not losing someone. It is the ordinary guilt of having been unkind to someone who trusted you, and then hiding from it until the hiding becomes who you are. The game argues that "never mind" is the heaviest thing a child can carry, that nobody clears a lump in their own throat alone, and that a real apology is one you send without knowing whether it will be answered. Every system expresses this. Feelings held in grow strong and distorted, feelings said aloud help other people, and only a friend who listens can unclog you.
pitch:heart-first.hidden_truth:
**The friendship.** Nell's best friend since age five was Tobias "Bix" Aldana, a gangly, fearless, slightly embarrassing boy. Only Nell called him Bix. Last June her mum Ruth, a postal carrier, was transferred when their town's sorting office closed.

**The talent show.** On the last Friday of term Bix went on stage and sang a going-away song he had written for Nell, on a red ukulele with a missing string. His voice cracked on the high note and the hall laughed. Cass Whitlow, the girl Nell had always wanted to impress, turned and looked at Nell. Nell was terrified of leaving as a nobody, so she laughed too, louder than anyone. At the coat pegs afterwards she did an impression of his cracked note and said "He's not really my friend, he just follows me around." Bix was standing behind the coats holding her goodbye present. She saw his shoes. Neither of them said a word. Three days later she moved without saying goodbye.

**The letters.** Nine letters arrived over the summer. Nell assumed they were full of hate and put each one unopened in a shoebox. They are not angry.

- Letter 1 says "I'm sorry I embarrassed you."
- Letters 2-7 are ordinary and funny: a drawing of a gull, news about his dog, a joke with the punchline on the next letter. They slowly get shorter.
- In letter 8 he signs "Tobias" instead of "Bix" for the first time.
- Letter 9 is the one she feared most: "I think my letters might be making it harder for you, so this is the last one. You were my best friend the whole time. Even that day. – Tobias."

**What the Sorting really is.** It is Nell's own invention. The Bix who lives there is the Bix she wishes she had left behind, one who was never hurt. He cannot hold hurt feelings, cannot remember June, and cannot sing. Mister Nevermind, the rubber-stamp-headed postman who voids everything near the truth, is not a monster. He is the part of Nell that decided she is "the kind of friend who laughs" and must therefore never have friends again, for their safety. The real Tobias never appears on screen and his forgiveness is never promised.
pitch:heart-first.emotional_arc:
The arc moves through five stages.

1. **Comfort.** The Sorting is funny and warm, Bix is perfect, and the player falls for him in five minutes.
2. **Itch.** Bix goes silent whenever there is music. The real world is grey pencil, and Nell answers every kindness with "never mind."
3. **Unease.** The bright world ends at a red ruled margin, and beyond it is erased paper and a floating crayon HA HA. Bix will not cross the line. Each opened letter is a small shock because it is kind.
4. **Reckoning.** On a crayon stage the game asks the player to press the button and laugh, and waits as long as it takes. Bix gains his first hurt feeling and finally sings. He says "I'm not him. He's better than me. He gets hurt," and lets her go.
5. **Healing.** Nell stops needing to be forgiven before she acts. She listens to Mister Nevermind, thanks him, and outgrows him. Colour returns to the real town one crayon at a time, and she waves back at the boy from the bakery.

The warmth the player is left with is that you are not the worst thing you did, provided you stop hiding from it.
pitch:heart-first.protagonist:
**Nell Tarrow, 11.** She is watchful, dry-witted and quick to help, and quicker to say "never mind." She narrates item descriptions with deadpan jokes. She believes she is secretly a bad friend and keeps everyone at arm's length to protect them.

- **Body and face:** Short and round-cheeked, with a freckled nose and dot eyes.
- **Hair:** A dark brown bob with a crooked fringe she cut herself.
- **Clothes:** A mustard-yellow raincoat two sizes too big, with sleeves covering her hands. A grey pleated skirt, navy-and-white striped socks that are always slipping, and red wellington boots.
- **Signature item:** Her mum's old olive canvas mail satchel with a brass buckle and a white enamel pigeon pin.
- **Two worlds:** In the real world she is drawn in graphite with a faint yellow wash. In the Sorting the raincoat is blazing crayon yellow and the satchel is comically huge.
- **Portrait expressions:** Neutral, small smile, looking away ("never mind"), startled, crying with a smile.

**Battle role:** An all-rounder whose skills move feelings between allies. She is the only one who can LISTEN to enemies from turn one.

**Skills:**
- First-Class (single hit)
- Forwarding Address (pass 2 tokens to an ally)
- Read Between Lines (reveal 1 address slot)
- Paper Plane (hit all)
- Hand-Deliver (the next SAY counts double for an address)
- P.S. (act again at half power)
- Dear — (ultimate; party-wide Glad +1 and a 25% heal)
party_members:
**BIX (the dream Bix)** appears 11.
- **Personality:** Sunshine-loud and generous. He invents rules to games mid-game and never holds a grudge, because he cannot.
- **Look:** Tall and skinny with warm brown skin, a puff of curly black hair and a gap-toothed grin. He wears a teal windbreaker with an orange zip, rust corduroy trousers with a star patch on the left knee, and white sneakers with one lace always untied.
- **Signature item:** A red ukulele with only three strings on his back. He never plays it.
- **Arc:** He slowly notices the holes in himself. He cannot remember June, cannot cross the red margin, and cannot sing. He realises he is Nell's wish, not her friend, and chooses to say goodbye so she can write to the real one.
- **Battle role:** Fast buffer and cheerleader who generates Glad.
- **Mechanical secret:** His tray cannot hold Sore. Any Sore he would gain lands on Nell as a Lump instead. In Chapter 7 he gains his first Sore and unlocks Cracked Note, his strongest skill.
- **Skills:** Race You! (party speed up), Best Day Ever (give an ally 2 Glad), Made-Up Rule (swap an enemy's two tokens), High Five (combo hit with Nell), Encore (repeat an ally's last skill), Cracked Note (late game; SAY Sore at triple strength).

**DAME MAGS, Complaint of the First Class.** She is one of 212 unsent complaint letters that an old lady wrote to the council about a pothole. Her real-world echo is Magda Wrona, 12, Nell's neighbour who shouts at puddles.
- **Personality:** Furious, formal and secretly tender. She drafts a complaint about every bench ("Dear Sir or Madam, this bench is ADEQUATE and I resent it").
- **Look:** Small and stocky with two tight ginger braids sticking out sideways and round red-framed glasses. Her cape is a cream envelope flap with a red-and-blue airmail border. She wears a tartan pinafore and pink galoshes.
- **Signature item:** A fountain pen as tall as she is, carried like a lance.
- **Arc:** She discovers the old lady kept complaining because the council clerk was the only person who ever wrote back. Her anger was loneliness in a hat. She learns to Say Sore instead of Cross.
- **Battle role:** Heavy hitter and taunter who builds Cross fast.
- **Skills:** Strongly Worded (big hit, self Cross +2), To Whom It May Concern (taunt), Underline (defence break), In Triplicate (three hits), Yours Faithfully (convert all her Cross to Sore and shield the party), Final Draft (ultimate; damage scales with the total tokens held by the whole party).

**NOLL.** He is a birthday card sent to a boy who had already moved away, stamped ADDRESS UNKNOWN. His real-world echo is Ollie Pryce, 10, the baker's son who waves at Nell every morning.
- **Personality:** Gentle, slow and apologetic. He is perpetually celebrating a birthday that ended months ago and is scared that once the party stops no one will remember him.
- **Look:** Tall, soft and round, with pale skin and sandy hair flopping over his eyes. He wears a blue paper party hat with gold stars on an elastic strap, an oversized lavender cardigan with balloon-shaped buttons, and mismatched socks (one green, one spotted).
- **Signature item:** A single half-deflated yellow balloon on a string tied to his wrist.
- **Arc:** He learns that a late card still counts and that being remembered is not the same as being on time. He lets go of the balloon himself.
- **Battle role:** Healer and wall who naturally holds Scared and turns it into protection.
- **Skills:** Read the Envelope (3 Ink; reveals an enemy's full address), Slice of Cake (heal), Many Happy Returns (revive at 40%), Blow Out the Candles (cleanse the party), Party Popper (blind all enemies), Hold My Balloon (take hits for an ally for 2 turns), Make a Wish (ultimate; a full-party heal that removes 1 Lump each and is usable once per battle).
pitch:heart-first.world_structure:
The game has three layers and 13 maps. Every map is built from ground materials plus placed props.

**1. Gullhaven (real, daytime)**
- **Look:** Graphite pencil and grey-blue watercolour wash on paper, with almost no colour.
- **Maps:**
  - (a) The Tarrow flat and the old sorting office below it. Props are moving boxes, the bed with the shoebox, brass pigeonhole racks, and a mail chute hatch in the floor.
  - (b) High Street and Seawall. The ground is cross-hatched wet pavement and slate. Props are the bakery, Magda's gate, a chip-stealing gull and the red pillar postbox at the seawall's end.
  - (c) Saltgate Primary gate and yard.
- **Colour returns:** Each letter Nell opens permanently adds one crayon colour to Gullhaven, in nine steps. The first is the postbox red and the last is the sea.

**2. The Sorting (dream, night)**
- **Look:** Saturated crayon and coloured pencil.
- **How you get there:** At bedtime Nell drops through the mail chute.
- **Maps:**
  - (d) Pigeonhole Plaza, the hub. The ground is cream envelope-paper cobbles and parcel-paper paths. Props are shelf-towers, postboxes with faces, twine fences and a vending machine that sells only envelopes.
  - (e) Stampwood. The grass is green blotting paper and the trees are giant perforated postage stamps on stick trunks.
  - (f) The Commissioner's Bureau. Pigeon civil servants work among queue ropes and towers of forms.
  - (g) Blotter Beach. The sand is pink blotter and the sea is ink with pen-stroke waves.
  - (h) Party Pier on Inkwell Lake. Bunting, a cake nobody has cut and empty chairs.
  - (i) Council Chambers. The floor is carbon-paper black, with filing-cabinet walls and rubber-stamp pillars.
  - (j) Dead-Letter Depot. Corrugated cardboard, conveyor belts and parcel cliffs.

**3. The Margin (the uneasy layer)**
- **How you get there:** Every dream map ends at a ruled red margin line. Step over it and the crayon stops.
- **Maps:**
  - (k) The Margin. Bare white paper with faint blue rules, eraser crumbs, half-rubbed-out props and Nell's own crossed-out handwriting on the ground.
  - (l) The Stage. A crayon school hall.
  - (m) The Shoebox. Cardboard cathedral walls, a tissue-paper floor and nine house-sized sealed envelopes as doors.

Benches appear in all three layers. They are the save points and the places where the party LISTENS.
chapter_outline: **PROLOGUE, 'First-Class' (5 min).** The game opens cold in full colour. Nell and Bix are on a hill of envelopes, racing paper planes. A tutorial battle against a Junk Mailer teaches HOLD and SAY, with Bix heckling ("Say it like you MEAN it, Tarrow!"). He starts to hum a tune and all sound cuts out. Nell wakes in a grey flat full of boxes. When the player examines the shoebox under the bed, the [Open it] option is scribbled out and only [Never mind] remains. Mum asks "Heard from Tobias?" and Nell answers "Never mind."

**CH1, Day One: Gullhaven.** Nell helps Mum re-deliver four misaddressed letters, a delivery puzzle that teaches the town. Magda is shouting at a pothole, and Ollie waves from the bakery. The first key choice appears: wave back, or never mind. There is a comic miniboss, Gerald the gull, who steals Mum's chips. At bedtime the chute hatch is glowing.

**CH2, Night One: Pigeonhole Plaza and Stampwood.** The pigeon bureaucracy demands Form 27-B, "Application to Feel Feelings." Mags joins after complaining her way into the party. The Stampwood fold-maze follows, then the boss, Commissioner Coo, who takes a lunch break mid-fight. Letter 1 is found in his out-tray. At the first bench there is the option to open it: "I'm sorry I embarrassed you." Bix says "Who's Tobias?" and laughs.

**CH3, Day Two: Saltgate Primary.** It is Nell's first day. A classmate does an impression of the teacher, everyone laughs, and the battle tray UI silently appears over the grey classroom while a Lump drops into Nell's tray. Ollie offers half a bun, which is the second key choice. After school Magda says "You're the girl who never waves."

**CH4, Night Two: Blotter Beach and Party Pier.** A birthday party is laid out for no one. Noll joins. The ink-footprint puzzle comes next. Whenever anyone sings Happy Birthday, Bix freezes like a skipped record. The boss is the Confetti Queen, a party-sized paper shredder who 'tidies up' forgotten cards. Letters 2-4 are found here, and they are funny and kind. One holds half a joke and the punchline arrives in Letter 5.

**CH5, Over the Red Line.** While chasing Noll's balloon, Nell steps past the margin. The map turns to blank ruled paper with eraser smudges, a mirror-writing room and the first encounter with The Laugh, a smiling crayon HA HA that follows her. Bix stands on the coloured side with his arm out, smiling, and will not cross. Nell wakes with a gasp.

**CH6, Day Three: Rain.** While unpacking, Mum finds the shoebox. She does not open it. She leaves it on Nell's bed with a book of stamps and a note: "In case you want to write back. No rush, love." This is the third key choice. Nell delivers a misrouted reply from the council to Magda's gran, the first answer that pothole ever got. Magda invites her to see the pothole, which is the fourth key choice.

**CH7, Night Three: Council Chambers, Depot, Stage.**
- **Mags's boss:** The Council, a three-headed stamp desk with heads marked APPROVED, DENIED and PENDING.
- **The Dead-Letter Depot:** A conveyor sorting puzzle, with Letters 5-8 to find.
- **The Stage:** The talent show is replayed as a crayon play. The player gets three options, and all three say "laugh" in fainter and fainter pencil. The game waits as long as the player needs.
- **The coat pegs:** A pair of shoes is visible behind the coats.
- **Bix's goodbye:** Bix gains his first Sore, sings one cracked verse and says goodbye at the Shoebox door. He stays in the party for one last fight.

**CH8, The Shoebox and the Morning After.**
- **Postmark puzzle:** The nine envelope doors must be put in postmark order.
- **Final battle:** The party fights Mister Nevermind, and one of the three endings is decided.
- **Epilogue:** The playable epilogue is set in Gullhaven at dawn, at the seawall postbox. This is the fifth key choice. Magda and Ollie are waiting with bikes.
- **Credits:** They roll over the stamp album.
pitch:heart-first.emotion_mechanic:
**THE HEART TRAY: Hold, Say, Swallow, Listen**

There is no emotion triangle and no type advantage. Feelings are physical tokens that you accumulate, carry, spend and get clogged by.

**Layout.** Enemies stand on a giant sheet of lined paper filling the top two-thirds of the screen. The party appears as four stamp-shaped cards along the bottom edge, like stamps on an envelope. Under each card is a perforated strip of 5 slots, which is that character's Heart Tray. Turn order runs as a postmark ribbon across the top. The command menu unfolds as a letter. HP is Heart and skill points are Ink.

**Gaining tokens.** A character can hold several kinds at once.
- **Sore (blue):** Gained by taking a single hit of at least 20% max Heart, or when an ally falls.
- **Cross (red):** Gained when your attack misses or is blocked, or when the same enemy targets you twice running.
- **Scared (violet):** Gained when an enemy telegraphs a Blurt, or when you drop below 30% Heart.
- **Glad (yellow):** Gained by landing a finishing blow, being healed or Listened to by an ally, or receiving a Said Glad.

Some skills add tokens on purpose.

**HOLD (passive, per token).**
- Glad: +5% crit and +1 Ink per turn.
- Sore: +10% defence, -5% speed.
- Cross: +12% attack, -8% defence.
- Scared: +10% evasion, -10% attack.

Bonuses stack up to 5. When the tray is full, the character is Brimming. Any new feeling pushes out the oldest token and turns it into a Lump.

**SAY (costs the turn).** Spend all n tokens of one kind on one target.
- **Glad to an ally:** Heals 12% Heart × n and gives them 1 Glad.
- **Sore to an ally:** Both gain a shield worth 8% × n.
- **Sore to an enemy:** Its attack drops 8% × n for 3 turns.
- **Cross to an enemy:** Deals damage of ATK × (1 + 0.6n). At n ≥ 3 it ignores defence.
- **Scared to an ally:** Both gain +10% × n evasion, and the ally acts next.
- **Scared to an enemy:** Reveals its next move. At n ≥ 3 the enemy hesitates and skips a turn.

**SWALLOW (the panic button).** The character gains a -60% damage Guard and status immunity this turn. All held tokens crush into Lumps, 1 Lump per 2 tokens, rounded up.
- A Lump is a grey token that blocks a slot and costs -1 Ink regen.
- At 3 Lumps the character is Choked and cannot SAY or use feeling skills.
- Lumps persist after battle.
- You cannot clear your own Lumps.

**LISTEN (costs the listener's turn).**
- On an ally, it removes 1 Lump, or 2 if the listener holds at least 2 Glad. Both gain 1 Glad and the listener regains 5 Ink.
- On an enemy, it removes 1 of its tokens, cancels a pending Blurt and reveals one address slot. Enemies have 3-slot trays and unleash a Blurt super-attack the turn after their tray fills.

**Benches and items.** A bench conversation clears all ordinary Lumps. Mum's Flask of Tea, of which only 3 exist in the game, clears 1 Lump mid-battle.

**Story Lumps.** Each real-world "Never mind" choice, of which there are 5, gives Nell a permanent Story Lump. Only opening one of Bix's letters removes it. Ignoring the letters literally chokes her.
pitch:heart-first.nonviolent_mechanic:
**DELIVER**

Every enemy is a message that never arrived. Each has an Address of 2-4 feeling symbols in order. For example, the Junk Mailer's is Glad-Glad-Glad and Final Notice's is Scared-Cross-Sore. The symbols show as "?" until revealed.

**How to reveal an address**
- Noll's Read the Envelope skill (3 Ink)
- LISTENing to the enemy
- Tells in enemy dialogue
- The Stamp Album, which remembers every address once it has been seen

**How it works**
- SAYing the correct next feeling at the enemy fills that slot, and any stack size counts.
- A stack of n ≥ 3 also stuns the enemy for 1 turn.
- A wrong feeling does not reset progress but hands the enemy 1 token of that kind, pushing it toward a Blurt.
- When the address is complete, the envelope opens. The enemy speaks one line of its message ("Dear Occupant: I only wanted ANYONE to be excited to see me") and leaves, Delivered.

**Rewards**
- A Delivered enemy gives the same Mileage (experience) as a defeat, plus 1 Stamp for the 32-stamp Album. Stamps unlock skills at 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 and also unlock new bench conversations. Delivered enemies drop few Scraps (currency).
- Tearing an enemy up (reducing its Heart to 0) drops double Scraps and no Stamp.

Neither route is scolded for regular foes. Fighting builds the tokens you need for delivering, so most battles blend both.

**Bosses**
- A Delivered boss moves into Pigeonhole Plaza as a cheerful NPC, and its area regains colour.
- A Torn boss leaves its area greyer, with an empty chair.
- Mister Nevermind's address is Scared-Sore-Cross-Glad. The Sore must be Said by Bix and the Glad by Nell.
endings:
**ENDING A, 'Return to Sender'.**
- **Condition:** Nell has opened 4 or fewer of the 8 findable letters when she reaches the Shoebox. This usually means she enters Choked by Story Lumps.
- **What happens:** The final battle is unwinnable but gentle. Mister Nevermind stamps the box VOID, tucks her in and says "It's fine. Never mind." Nell wakes and pushes the shoebox to the back of the wardrobe. Gullhaven stays grey. Then Magda knocks with a misdelivered parcel, and the last image is Nell's hand on the latch, the door opening a crack, with one line of colour coming through. The closing text reads "Some letters wait."
- **New Game+:** Keeps the Album and adds a faint hum on the title screen.

**ENDING B, 'Postage Due'.**
- **Condition:** Either 5-7 letters opened, or 8 opened but Mister Nevermind is Torn by force instead of Delivered.
- **What happens:** Letter 9 is found in his empty coat and is readable. Nell writes Tobias a four-page letter, mostly explanations of why it wasn't really her fault, and posts it. The town is half-coloured. She bikes with Magda and Ollie and means it, but she still glances at the postbox.
- **Tone:** Bittersweet and honest. It is an apology that is still partly about herself. No reply is shown.

**ENDING C, 'Dear Bix,' (true).**
- **Condition:** All 8 letters opened, Mister Nevermind Delivered in the order Scared, Sore (from Bix), Cross, Glad (from Nell), and Bix's goodbye accepted.
- **What happens:** Nevermind kneels, hands over Letter 9 ("I kept this one longest") and holds his umbrella over her until she finishes reading. Then he folds himself into an ordinary postman's cap. The player composes Nell's letter from phrase-stamps gathered in the Album. It is short and cannot fit excuses: "I laughed. It was the worst thing I've done. You don't have to write back." She posts it at dawn. A montage of seasons shows Gullhaven in full colour, Nell waving first, and the three kids at the pothole.
- **Final shot:** In Mum's delivery bag there is a postcard with a doodled gull and unfamiliar-familiar handwriting: "Dear Nell —". The game cuts to the title before we can read more. The full song plays for the first time and resolves on its last note.
signature_images: **Title / CG1.** A shoebox under a bed in a grey graphite bedroom, with a seam of blazing crayon colour leaking from under its lid across the floorboards.
**CG2.** Nell and Bix on a hill of envelopes, launching paper planes into a sky tiled with postage stamps. His shoelace is untied and her sleeves cover her hands.
**CG3.** Nell falling down the brass mail chute, her pencil-grey body filling with crayon colour from the boots upward.

**CG4.** The Lost Letter Club on a bench at night. Mags is scribbling a complaint about the bench, Noll's balloon is sagging, Nell is half-smiling, and Bix is staring at nothing, the ukulele untouched.

**CG5.** The red margin line. Lush crayon grass ends dead at a ruled red line, and beyond it is blank paper with eraser smudges. Bix stands on the coloured side with his arm outstretched, smiling and not stepping over.
**CG6.** The talent show. A small boy with a red ukulele stands in a crayon spotlight. The audience is a crowd of faceless HA HA speech bubbles, and one bubble rises from the viewer's own position.
**CG7.** The coat pegs. Rows of hanging coats, with a pair of white sneakers visible beneath them, one lace untied, and a wrapped present held at knee height.
**CG8.** Bix finally singing, mouth open mid-crack, with one tear. His colours run like wet watercolour at the edges.
**CG9.** Mister Nevermind on one knee in the cardboard cathedral. His rubber-stamp head is cracked, and he holds a black umbrella over tiny Nell as she reads the last letter.
**CG10.** Dawn at the seawall. Nell is on tiptoes, posting a letter into the red pillar box, and Magda and Ollie are waiting with bikes. The sea is the last thing to turn blue.
enemy_concepts: **Junk Mailer.** A grinning glossy flyer shouting YOU MAY HAVE ALREADY WON. Its address is Glad-Glad-Glad, because it only wants someone excited.
**Chain Letter.** A paper-chain snake that threatens seven years of bad luck and then apologises for the tone. Its address is Scared-Glad.
**Papercut.** A tiny, sharp origami swan that is fast and spiteful. Its address is Cross-Sore.
**Lick the Stamp Snail.** It glues your tokens in place so they cannot be Said for 2 turns.
**Final Notice.** A red envelope with stern eyebrows that gets Scared itself when you Listen to it.
**Pen Pal-tergeist.** The ghost of a letter that only ever got as far as 'Dear'. It copies the last feeling Said in the battle.
**Inkblot.** A Rorschach blob that asks 'What do you see?'. Its address changes to mirror your own tray.
**Paperclip Crab.** It pinches two party members together so they share damage.
**Rubber Band Bandit.** It snaps your oldest token back at you as damage.
**Postcard Gull.** It has WISH YOU WERE HERE written on its wings. It inflicts Sore across the party and wants Sore Said back to it.
**Wrong Number.** A ringing crayon telephone that never speaks. It can only be Delivered by Listening 3 times.
**Blank Card.** It has no address at all, so you must give it one by Saying any three feelings, and it becomes whatever you said.
**Eraser Mite (Margin).** It rubs out one held token per turn and leaves pink crumbs.
**Crossed-Out (Margin).** A scribbled-over word on legs. The word underneath flickers between 'sorry' and 'stay'.
**The Laugh (Margin).** A smiling floating HA HA that drops Lumps into trays. It cannot be hurt. It can only be outlasted or Listened to until it becomes a very small 'ha'.

**BOSSES.**
- **Commissioner Coo:** A pigeon bureaucrat who takes a lunch break at 50% Heart. His forms must be 'filled' with the correct feelings.
- **The Confetti Queen:** A party-sized shredder in a paper crown who believes forgetting is tidy.
- **The Council:** A three-headed stamp desk marked APPROVED, DENIED and PENDING. The PENDING head never acts until it is Listened to.
- **Mister Nevermind:** A tall postman with a rubber-stamp head whose face is the mirror-written word VOID. He voids tokens, turns Says into Lumps and says 'It's fine' before every attack.
- **Gerald:** The real-world comic miniboss, a chip-thieving gull.
pitch:heart-first.antagonistic_force:
**MISTER NEVERMIND.** He is a towering, soft-spoken postman in a long navy coat with brass buttons. His head is a rubber stamp and he carries a black umbrella. He patrols the Sorting stamping VOID on any path, memory or NPC that gets near June, and he is why Bix cannot remember or sing.

He is not cruel. He is Nell's avoidance, hardened into a conviction: "You are the kind of friend who laughs. Best not to have friends. It's fine. Never mind." He speaks only in reassurances, and that is what makes him frightening.

His outriders are the Margin creatures: erasers, crossed-out words and The Laugh. The real antagonist is the phrase itself, which the player chooses again and again in the real world because it is always the easiest option on the menu. The game quietly counts each time.

He is defeated not by destruction but by being heard and thanked. He kept the ninth letter safe, and he hands it over himself.
pitch:heart-first.exploration_and_puzzles:
**Exploration rhythm.** Days are small, grey and tender. They hold chores, neighbours and key choices. Nights are large, bright and full of secrets.

**Puzzles**
1. **Misdelivered Mail (Gullhaven).** Match four smudged addresses to houses using clues from neighbour gossip.
2. **Stampwood Fold-Maze.** Tear along perforated lines to fold map corners over, changing which paths connect.
3. **Ink Footprints (Blotter Beach).** Your steps leave ink, and you must walk the shape of the letter a riddle asks for without crossing your own line.
4. **Mirror Room (Margin).** Everything is reversed like a rubber stamp's face. Controls and signs are mirrored, and the answer is read in a puddle.
5. **Depot Conveyor.** Route parcels to pigeonholes by switching belts. This is a light logic-grid puzzle.
6. **Postmark Order (Shoebox).** Arrange the nine envelope doors by date, using Mum's route sheet and the kitchen calendar from the real world.

**Benches.** They handle saving, clearing Lumps, optional letter-opening scenes and unlockable banter. Mags files a complaint about each bench, and there are 11 collectible complaints.

**The Stamp Album.** It holds 32 stamps. It doubles as a bestiary that stores addresses and as the phrase bank for the final letter.

**Items (about 20)**
- Lemon Sherbet: heals 40 Heart.
- Bubble Wrap: a shield, and Nell must pop one first.
- Second-Class Stamp: slow heal over time.
- Ink Cartridge: restores 15 Ink.
- Sticky Label: locks an enemy token in place.
- Return Slip: escape from battle.
- Birthday Candle: revive.
- Gerald's Chip: bait.
- Mum's Flask of Tea: clears 1 Lump.

**Secrets**
- The Margin can be entered from the edge of any dream map. It holds hidden rooms containing Nell's crossed-out drafts.
- New Game+ carries over the Album and adds address variants.
pitch:heart-first.humor_and_charm:
**The pigeon civil service.** The Sorting is run by pigeons, who are deeply unionised.
- They issue Form 27-B, "Application to Feel Feelings," with three questions and one of them "coo."
- They close battles for lunch.
- They award Nell a lanyard reading VISITOR (PROBABLY).

**Running gags**
- Mags writes complaints to everything: benches, the moon, the save prompt ("Dear Game, I did not consent to being saved").
- Noll apologises to enemies before healing them by mistake.
- Bix invents rules mid-battle ("New rule: crits count double if you yell"). They do not count double. He yells anyway.
- The vending machine sells only envelopes and is very proud of its range.
- The Chain Letter's threats get more polite each turn.
- Gerald the gull has a full boss intro, a health bar and one hit point.
- Nell's deadpan inspect text covers every prop ("A pothole. Magda has named it. Its name is Kevin.").

**Warmth.** Mum's terrible postal puns. The baker's son waving every single morning whether or not you wave back. When a boss is Delivered, it moves into the Plaza and takes up a hobby.

**Pacing.** The jokes thin out as the Margin approaches and return, quieter, in the epilogue.
pitch:heart-first.music_direction:
**Overall.** There are 14 tracks, composed as MIDI and rendered with a General MIDI soundfont.
- **Lo-fi treatment:** Tape wow and flutter, vinyl crackle and a low-pass at about 9 kHz.
- **Margin treatment:** Extra bitcrush and reversed reverb on Margin tracks.
- **Real-world treatment:** Real-world tracks are nearly dry.

**Leitmotif, 'Bix's Song'.** In C major the phrase is G4-A4-C5-A4-G4-E4-D4. It always stops on the unresolved D (re). It resolves to C only in the true ending. Every track hides it, whether inverted, reharmonised, reversed or as a bassline.

**Tracks**
1. **'Dear —' (title).** Solo music box plays the motif, which cuts off after the 6th note.
2. **'First-Class Morning' (Plaza).** Ukulele-style nylon plucks, glockenspiel and brushed kit at 112 bpm.
3. **'Gullhaven, Overcast'.** Felt piano, distant strings and rain. The motif is in the left hand only.
4. **'Stampwood Shuffle'.** Nylon guitar, celesta and walking bass.
5. **'Licked & Sealed' (battle).** Square lead, slap bass and kit at 150 bpm. The motif is inverted.
6. **'Please Hold' (Bureau and Coo).** Cheesy bossa muzak with organ and a hold-tone beep.
7. **'Many Happy Returns' (Pier).** Toy piano and a kazoo-like saw lead, slightly detuned, with Happy-Birthday-adjacent phrases that never finish.
8. **'Red Line' (Margin).** Reversed music box, a choir pad and a sub drone. The motif is played backwards.
9. **'Strongly Worded' (boss).** Saw lead over a strings ostinato in 7/8.
10. **'Bench'.** A 30-second nylon guitar lullaby.
11. **'Ha Ha' (Stage).** Celesta and pizzicato that thin out instrument by instrument until only a metronome is left.
12. **'Never Mind' (final).** Piano, choir and kit, with the motif fighting itself in two keys. On Delivery everything drops out to the music box.
13. **'Dear Bix,' (true ending).** The full song at last. It is played with three-note chords only, because the ukulele has three strings. The melody cracks once on purpose and then resolves.
14. **'Postage Due' (credits for endings A and B).** Piano and strings. The motif is unresolved.

**Sound effects (about 25)**
- Rubber-stamp thunk (confirm)
- Envelope tear (cancel)
- Pencil scratch (text)
- Paper rustle (menu)
- Pigeon coo
- Token clink, one pitch per feeling
- Lump thud
- Listen chime
- Blurt warning
- Chute whoosh
- Bench creak
- Stamp-lick
- Balloon squeak
- Gull cry
- Letter-open flutter
pitch:heart-first.originality_notes:
**Versus OMORI.** There is no shut-in, no death and no hidden tragedy involving a sibling. The secret is a small, survivable cruelty, and the person wronged is alive and kind. Feelings are not a three-way advantage wheel. They are stackable mixed tokens that are held, spent, swallowed into Lumps and cleared only by a friend's LISTEN. The battle layout is a bottom row of stamp cards beneath a sheet of lined paper, with no corner portraits. The dream friend knows he is a wish and chooses to leave.

**Versus Undertale.** There is no underground, no fallen human and no kill-counter morality. Sparing does not run through a menu of acts. DELIVER is an ordered feeling-address puzzle fed by the same tokens that fighting generates, growth is equal on both routes, and endings hinge on opening the letters, not on body counts.

**Versus End Roll.** There is no punishment dream, no drug trial and no crimes of violence. The dream is self-made comfort, guilt is scaled to real childhood, and the cast is never killed off for shock.

**Versus Ib.** There is no gallery and no cursed artworks. The paper-and-post world comes from the mail theme, the colour-returning real world is the visual through-line, and there is no rose-style health object.

**Versus Re:Kinder.** There is no pact among children and no town massacre. The darkness is psychological and gentle, with no gore, and the humour comes from pigeon bureaucracy, not shock.

**Shared tradition only.** A bright world over a painful truth, turn-based party battles, cute-creepy contrast and multiple endings.

**Original pillars.** The postal metaphor (unsent, void, deliver, return to sender), the Lump-and-Listen interdependence, Story Lumps linking real-world dialogue choices to battle, letters that restore colour one crayon at a time, a leitmotif that refuses to resolve until the apology is sent, and a final boss who is thanked.

pitch:imagery-first.title: PENCIL ME IN: A Thimble Hill Story
pitch:imagery-first.logline: In the last week before her forgetful grandmother's seaside house is sold, 11-year-old Nell falls into the unfinished picture book Oma drew for her. It is a crayon town of lost household things, and something polite is rubbing it out page by page. To save it she must find out who is holding the eraser.
pitch:imagery-first.theme_statement: You can rub out the line, but not the groove it left in the paper. Love that gets forgotten still happened. Being forgotten by someone is not the same as never having been loved by them, and turning up anyway is a way of remembering for two.
pitch:imagery-first.hidden_truth:
Oma (Odile Brandt, 78) illustrated the Thimble Hill picture books. She has dementia. Two winters ago, during a confused spell, she did not recognise Nell in her own hallway. She took her for an intruder and screamed at her to get out. Nell, then 9, ran. Afterwards she told her dad, Joss, that "Oma said she doesn't want me there," which was a lie told out of hurt, and she refused every visit for a year and a half.

During that time Oma still had clear months. She asked for Nell every week and wrote her letters she never managed to post. She began a last book, "The Last Lamplight", dedicated "for Nell, so I don't lose you". Its star was Blot, an ink spill that toddler Nell once made on a finished illustration. Oma kept the spill, drew a face on it, and called it "my best mistake".

Now Oma no longer asks for anyone. The house on Marram Lane is being packed up and she moves to a care home on Saturday.

The thing erasing the book is not the illness. It is the Tidy, a neat white paper-cutout child with Nell's exact silhouette. It comes from Nell's own wish: "forget her first, before she finishes forgetting me; it hurts less if the page is clean." On her first night back, Nell really did take a pink eraser to the book.

Each boss is one of Oma's hard memories, drawn by a hand that was losing its skill. The third boss, the terrifying Stranger-in-the-Hall, is Oma's drawing of Nell on that winter day, seen through frightened eyes. Under every erased patch lies the Underdrawing, Oma's first blue-pencil sketch layer, where the true memories survive as grooves in the paper. The game never treats the illness as a villain. As one character puts it, "The sea isn't being cruel to the sand."
pitch:imagery-first.emotional_arc:
1. **Monday.** Nell is numb, dry and polite, and she tidies compulsively. Oma offers her the same biscuit three times, which is funny and hurts.
2. **Chapters 1-2.** She takes delight in the book world and lets herself love Oma's drawings again.
3. **Late chapter 2.** Unease sets in as props and townsfolk vanish overnight, matching what Nell threw out while packing that day.
4. **Chapter 3.** She reaches for anger and blame ("it's the illness, it's not fair"). Then comes the midpoint shock: the monster in the hall is a drawing of her.
5. **Chapter 4.** Guilt arrives with the unsent letters. Grief follows as Blot fades while Nell holds her hand.
6. **Chapter 5.** She confesses the lie in the Underdrawing and faces the Tidy as herself, a neat face with no mouth.
7. **Saturday.** She accepts that Oma may never know her name again, and decides whether to show up regardless.

Every ending leaves Nell with something she cannot erase.
pitch:imagery-first.protagonist:
**Nell Brandt, age 11.** She is watchful and dry-humoured. She says "fine" when she is not fine, and she straightens and tidies things when upset, which quietly foreshadows the Tidy. She is left-handed like Oma. She speaks little, and the player picks her few lines.

**Appearance**
- Hair: a short, choppy dark-brown bob she cut herself, with a fringe cut too short.
- Face: round, freckles across the nose, and a graphite smudge on her right cheek and along the side of her left hand.
- Clothes: an oversized mustard-yellow raincoat with the sleeves rolled twice, over a navy-and-white striped shirt. Grey shorts. Red wellington boots, the left one patched with a square of silver tape.
- Signature item: Oma's stubby two-ended checking pencil, red at one end and blue at the other, tucked behind her left ear.

**Art style by layer**
- In the real world she is drawn in restrained graphite with muted watercolour-pencil.
- Inside the book she is redrawn in Oma's style, with dot eyes, rosy crayon-circle cheeks and thick wobbly outlines.

**Battle**
- Heart Color: Blue (Longing).
- Role: a flexible support attacker, and the only character with "Name It".
- Skills:
  - Underline: a blue hit that lowers the target's defence.
  - Read Aloud: a party shield.
  - Dog-Ear: marks an enemy so allies' attacks cannot miss it.
  - Name It.
party_members:
**Blot, mischievous trickster and the heart of the game.**

She introduces herself with "I'm a mistake! The best one. It says so right here..." and points at a caption that has been rubbed out. She makes puns about being "a stain on the family name". Secretly she is terrified that mistakes get corrected. In truth she is Oma's memory of Nell herself. Her arc runs from fear of being fixed to knowing she was kept on purpose.

- Heart Color: Yellow (Wonder).
- Battle role: the fastest unit, a status and mood manipulator.
- Skills:
  - Splat: a yellow hit with a chance to Smear, which lowers accuracy.
  - Peek: reveals an enemy's Heart Color and Missing Color.
  - Spill: pushes 2 strokes of a chosen color.
  - Seep: steals one buff.
- Appearance:
  - A child-shaped ink blot a head shorter than Nell, with a glossy blue-black body and splashy scalloped edges.
  - Three satellite droplets orbit her head like a hair bobble.
  - Two large white oval eyes with no pupils, and a small white crescent smile painted in correction fluid.
  - She leaves ink footprints that fade after four steps. When she fades, her outline turns to dotted line.
  - Signature item: a silver paperclip worn as a hairclip.

**Sir Tuppence, boastful tiny knight and comic relief.**

He narrates his own deeds in the third person and gets stuck in teacups. He is afraid that being small means he cannot protect anyone. He is Oma's drawing of her son Joss as a boy playing knights. Real Joss is exhausted, selling the house, and trying to "fix" everything. His arc is learning that protecting someone is not the same as fixing them. His final skill, "Stand Beside", replaces his "Stand In Front".

- Heart Color: Red (Nerve).
- Battle role: tank and taunter.
- Skills:
  - Needle Charge: a red hit.
  - Stand In Front: takes hits for one ally.
  - Boast: taunts, and pushes a red stroke.
  - Thimble Down: a big guard that reflects 30% of damage.
- Appearance:
  - A round little knight in a dented silver thimble helmet with a dimple pattern and a dark eye-slit showing two shining dot eyes.
  - A breastplate made from a green bottle cap and boots made from acorn cups.
  - A red-and-white checked tea-towel cape.
  - Signature item: a darning-needle lance trailing a long blue thread.

**Oddment ("Oddy"), gentle, fussing mender.**

He says "there, there" to furniture and apologises to enemies before hitting them. He is Oma's drawing of her late husband Emil, a tailor who mended everything. His arc comes when he cannot mend Blot as she fades. He learns that some tears cannot be stitched and can only be sat beside.

- Heart Color: Green (Tenderness, the Blue + Yellow blend). It is the hardest mood to hold and gives the biggest reward.
- Battle role: healer and shielder.
- Skills:
  - Stitch: a blue single-target heal.
  - Patch: cures a status and adds a shield, yellow.
  - There There: a party heal over time.
  - Darn It: a mallet hit, his only attack, which he is embarrassed about.
- Appearance:
  - A tall lop-eared rabbit sewn from odd socks, with an oatmeal wool body.
  - One ear is green argyle and one is red-striped.
  - Mismatched button eyes, the left a large tortoiseshell button and the right a small mother-of-pearl one. Half-moon spectacles hang on a thread.
  - A visibly darned patch over his heart in yellow thread.
  - He carries a pincushion satchel.
  - Signature item: a wooden darning mushroom used as a mallet.

**Dill, a late-game guest who joins in chapter 5.**

She is Oma as an 11-year-old, the book's author and lamplighter. She is bossy, bright and unsentimental ("Well, don't just stand there feeling things, draw!"). She takes Blot's battle slot if Blot was lost. Otherwise she acts as an assist every third round. Her arc is handing the pencil over.

- Heart Color: whatever the Page's current mood is, because she is the author.
- Battle role: a wildcard.
- Skills:
  - Lamplight: removes one Blank stroke and pushes any color.
  - First Draft: revives an ally at 30% HP.
  - Bold Line: a big hit in the current mood's color.
- Appearance:
  - Two tight ash-blonde plaits tied with green ribbons, round wire glasses and scabbed knees.
  - A paint-stained grey smock, too large, over a green gingham dress, with brown lace-up shoes.
  - A red/blue pencil behind her ear, identical to Nell's.
  - Her hands and feet are still uncoloured blue construction-pencil lines.
  - Signature item: a lamplighter's pole tipped with a glowing yellow crayon flame.
pitch:imagery-first.world_structure:
There are three layers, each with its own drawing style.

**1. Marram Lane (real world, days Monday to Saturday)**

Oma's seaside house is drawn in grey graphite with pale, muted watercolour-pencil. It is quiet and half-packed.

- Ground materials: floorboards, kitchen lino, hall runner carpet.
- Props: cardboard boxes, a biscuit tin, a drafting table, a doorframe with height marks, and a coat stand.
- Each day Nell packs one room. There are 15 memory objects in all, 3 per day, and she chooses Keep, Give away or Throw out for each. The Keep box holds only 6 across the whole game.
- Kept objects become equippable Keepsakes inside the book. Each one also unlocks one Underdrawing memory.
- Thrown-out objects are found rubbed out in the book that night.

**2. Thimble Hill (the book)**

This layer is saturated crayon and colored pencil on cream paper, a mouse-scale town of lost household things. Nell enters at night by opening the book at its ribbon bookmark. She moves between pages by peeling dog-eared page corners at the edges of maps.

- Quilt Fields: patchwork fabric ground, stitched paths, pin-tree forests and cotton-reel hay bales.
- Button Square (hub): button cobbles, teapot houses, a spool clock tower and a matchbox market.
- Teapot Row interiors: a shop, an inn and the cutlery council hall.
- Bathtub Harbor: white tile ground, soap-dish ferries, tap waterfalls and sponge islands.
- The Drain: a dark spiral of wet tile, chain and plug.
- The Staircase: giant wooden steps, one step per year. Height marks run up the wall and stop at "Nell, 9".
- Landing of Framed Faces: floral wallpaper, carpet runner and smudged portraits.
- Attic of Unsent Things: dusty boards, trunk-houses and envelopes strung on washing lines.

Erased areas appear as grey rubbed patches with faint ghost lines and crawling pink eraser crumbs.

**3. The Underdrawing**

Nell reaches it by shading a rubbed patch with the Graphite Stick. It is bare paper with blue construction lines, perspective grids and Oma's marginal notes in looping handwriting.

- True memories play out here as rough blue sketches.
- Its deepest part is the Margin. Beyond the Margin is the Last Page, a lamplit hill left unfinished.

**Map count**

| Layer | Maps |
|---|---|
| Marram Lane | 2 |
| Thimble Hill | 8 |
| Margin and Last Page | 2 |
| Total | 12 |
chapter_outline: **Prologue, Monday (10 min).** Nell and Dad arrive at Marram Lane. Oma politely asks whether she is "one of Joss's friends" and offers her the same biscuit three times. She hums a seven-note tune while drawing in spilled sugar with her finger. In the studio Nell finds "The Last Lamplight", half its pages rubbed grey. A blot on page 3 blinks at her. She falls in. Blot, sitting on a caption line, introduces herself as "the best mistake" and teaches the tutorial fight against a Dust Bunny. Nell can Finish it by drawing it a burrow.

**Chapter 1, Quilt Fields and Button Square (Monday night, 12 min).**
- Nell rescues Sir Tuppence from a teacup and meets the town. The cutlery council cannot pass a motion because the fork abstains. The shopkeeper is Mx. Best-Offer, a price tag.
- The game introduces the Swatch, Finishing and the Graphite Stick rubbing mechanic.
- Puzzle: sew the right buttons back onto the right coats.
- Boss: the Clock That Can't. All its numbers have slid to one side and it keeps asking what time it is.
- Underdrawing memory: Oma failing the clock-drawing test, and Dad crying in the car.

**Chapter 2, Bathtub Harbor and the Drain (Tuesday, 14 min).**
